name: sgs/responsive-logo
title: SGS Responsive Logo
description: Three-slot logo block (desktop / tablet / mobile) with optional SVG animation. Competitive moat: H/Square/Mark aspect-ratio variants per breakpoint.

fx._comment_providesNatively: Spec 38 FR-38-15 / §7. This block ALREADY exposes stroke-draw through its own `animationStyle` enum (draw-on-load | hover-redraw | scroll-trigger), whose values FR-38-15 keeps byte-identical across the Vivus->DrawSVG swap. Listing `draw` again in the generic 'Scroll & effects' picker would put TWO controls for ONE capability on this block, which this codebase bans. `generate-fx-qualifying-blocks.py` subtracts every effect named here from the block's derived roster, so the exclusion is a declaration this block OWNS rather than a per-block carve-out in the generator or in fx.js. Any future block that natively owns an fx capability declares it the same way.

wrapper.label: Wrapper
wrapper._note:
Root
(render.php get_block_wrapper_attributes, style.css .sgs-responsive-logo — display:inline-block hardcoded, no attribute, so no `layer`/arrangement members). Empty-string prefix resolves the bare width/maxWidth/maxHeight attrs case-insensitively via the default {suffix} convention (Width/MaxWidth/MaxHeight). No background-color/border/box-shadow/gap/aspect-ratio attribute or native support exists (no color/border supports declared on this block — logo images carry no theme-colour fill) — honest gaps. The / itself has no crop-box scenario (width:100%/max-width:100%, natural aspect) so supports.sgs.imageControls (universal image extension) was removed 2026-08-11 (Spec 35 capability-routing doctrine) as dead — the block's own per-device logoId*/logoUrl* art-direction tiers are its real media mechanism. logoId/logoIdTablet/logoIdMobile/svgAnimationSource/logoSwitchMode/animationStyle are media-source/behaviour scalars with no cluster member — deliberately undeclared (no prefix claims them).

image.label: Logo image
image._note: Declared 2026-09-05. This element did not exist in the manifest at all, so its attrs fell to the heuristic path and FOUR of them (width, alt, logoSwitchCustomPx, logoDecorative) were each assigned css_property='max-width' — two of which are not CSS at all (`alt` is a string, `logoDecorative` a boolean). render.php:239-240 shows the real and only owner of max-width is the `maxWidth` tier object. Declaring it here gives the slot its true owner via the manifest-first precedence (css_property = manifest_css_property or emission_css_property). Tested 2026-09-05: removing this element's empty-string prefix does NOT change the max-width over-match (still 8 contending attrs after a reseed), so the empty prefix is NOT the cause — the over-assignment is in the classifier's emission heuristic, not this manifest.

supports._comment_parallax: Parallax deliberately excluded — not appropriate for a header logo.

align._comment: FR-36-22 basics: explicit left-align default (NN/g: 6x better home-return). Plain string (no enum) mirrors WP core's auto-injected align attribute shape — matches the supports.align list above without a coercion risk (D291 gotcha: an out-of-enum stored value silently resets to default).

logoId._comment: Desktop/base logo — media library attachment ID. Renamed from desktopLogoId (2026-08-05): the base attr carries no tier suffix, matching the framework's universal responsive-tier convention (e.g. backgroundImage/backgroundImageTablet/backgroundImageMobile) instead of the old desktop/tablet/mobile PREFIX scheme, which was structurally invisible to the DB's modifier_suffixes tier-detection (a suffix strip, not a prefix strip).

logoUrl._comment: Media-library URL for this tier's logo, stored ALONGSIDE the attachment ID. Added 2026-08-05 so this block mirrors how every other SGS image block declares an image (sgs/media imageUrl+imageId, sgs/decorative-image, sgs/product-card): the ID wins at render and the URL is the fallback (media/render.php:467). WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the `image-alt` role pairs an alt attr to a SIBLING image attr via block_attributes.alt_companion_attr, and walk.py:295 only captures alt when that companion is attr_type='string'. With three bare attachment IDs (type=number) and no string image attr, there was nothing to name as the companion, so `alt` had to be routed through the interim `authored-alt-text` category. This attr is that companion.

logoSwitchMode._comment: When the compact/alternate logo replaces the desktop logo. mobile = at the mobile tier (<=767px viewport); tablet = at the tablet tier (<=1023px viewport); custom = at the operator's own breakpoint (<= logoSwitchCustomPx, viewport). Only takes effect once an alternate (mobile or tablet) logo is set.

svgAnimationSource._comment: Media library ID of a .svg file. NEVER accept inline SVG paste — XSS risk. Force upload via media library only.

logoDecorative._comment: WCAG 2.1 AA 1.1.1 explicit editorial decorative-image flag (mirrors sgs/timeline's milestoneMediaDecorative). Block-level, not per-tier: one flag covers the logo concept across logoId/logoIdTablet/logoIdMobile the same way `alt` already does. A site logo wrapped in a homepage link is almost never truly decorative — but this block sets the 's aria-label independently of the alt (see render.php's $link_aria_label), so the link keeps its accessible name ('Go to [Site] homepage') even when the logo image itself is marked decorative. render.php blanks alt + adds aria-hidden on the when true.
